content: 1. Artemether/lumefantrine reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Atazanavir may either increase or decrease the levels of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. 3. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of atogepant by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 4. Atorvastatin increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 5. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of axitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of bendamustine by reducing its metabolism. Bendamustine is minimally metabolized to active metabolites by CYP1A2. Ethinylestradiol, a weak CYP1A2 inhibitor, may increase bendamustine plasma concentrations when co-administered. Use caution and monitor. 7. Bosentan decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of caffeine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Carbamazepine decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Cefaclor reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 11. Cefadroxil reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 12. Cefazolin reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 13. Cefdinir reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 14. Cefepime reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 15. Cefepime/enmetazobactam reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. An additional or alternative form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 16. Cefixime reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 17. Cefotaxime reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 20. Ceftibuten reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 21. Cefuroxime reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 22. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Women should use additional or alternative non-hormonal birth control when using cenobamate with oral contraceptives. 23. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 24. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 26. Cephalexin reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 27. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Chloramphenicol reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 30. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Ciprofloxacin reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 32. Clarithromycin reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 33. Clindamycin reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 34. Clobazam reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be diminished when co-administered. Additional non-hormonal forms of contraception are recommended. 35. Clobazam reduces the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be diminished when co-administered. Additional non-hormonal forms of contraception are recommended. 36. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, thereby increasing serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. Use caution and monitor. 37. Crofelemer increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Crofelemer has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit systemically due to minimal absorption. Use caution and monitor. 38. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of cyclosporine by an unknown mechanism. Combined oral contraceptives containing ethinylestradiol may inhibit the metabolism and increase plasma concentrations of cyclosporine. Use caution and monitor. 39. Dabrafenib reduces the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 40. Dabrafenib reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 41. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by increasing plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates. Consider dose reduction of BCRP substrates according to their prescribing information. Use caution and monitor. 42. Dexamethasone reduces the levels of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Darunavir reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, and the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 44. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Deferasirox reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Demeclocycline reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 47. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of diazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, thereby increasing serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. Use caution and monitor. 48. Dicloxacillin reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 49. Doxycycline reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. 50. Efavirenz reduces the levels of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 51. Elafibranor reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Elafibranor, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce systemic exposure to hormonal contraceptives. Switch to effective non-hormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method if co-administered during elafibranor treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 52. Elagolix reduces the levels of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 53. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 54. Encorafenib affects the levels of levonorgestrel oral by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy of these agents. Use caution and monitor. 55. Encorafenib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP. Monitor for signs and symptoms of increased exposure and consider adjusting the dose of these substrates. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 56. Enzalutamide reduces the levels of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 57. Erythromycin base reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 58. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 59. Erythromycin lactobionate reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 60. Erythromycin stearate reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 61. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. Use caution and monitor. 62. Etravirine reduces the levels of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 63. Oral contraceptives may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Exenatide, which slows gastric emptying, may reduce the extent and rate of absorption of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide administration. Use caution and monitor.
